lines.en: What the law forbids and what the law punishes are two very different things.
It is one thing to hear the words, another to listen to them, and quite another to understand them.
The word 'home' carries a weight that 'house' was never built to bear.
Were the instructions any less precise, the machine would be not merely useless but dangerous.
Not until you try to translate a joke do you discover how much of its meaning lives outside the words.
However similar 'remember' and 'remind' may look, confusing them can change a message completely.
It is the difference between 'I did not say that' and 'I did not say that' - emphasis alone can move the meaning.
The contract states that payment is due 'within' thirty days, which is not the same as 'after' thirty days.
What a dictionary gives you is the skeleton of a word; its flesh and blood come from use.
Rarely does a mistranslation start a war, but history shows it has come uncomfortably close.
It is the context, not the dictionary, that decides which of a word's many meanings is alive in a sentence.
Were every word to carry only one meaning, poetry would be impossible and lawyers unemployed.
What separates 'almost right' from 'right' in translation is often a single syllable.
Not until the ambassador chose the wrong word did anyone realize the interpreter had been smoothing things over for years.
However precise a definition may be, real usage always finds a way to bend it.
